correctness.rationale: For mean-zero angular variations, the intermediate-coefficient first derivative is the discrete Fourier transform of root motion; Parseval gives n times squared deviations. Rotational orthogonality kills the second polynomial derivative term. For r>1 a beta-integral ratio A_{r-2}/A_r=r/[4(r-1)] yields nr/8. For 0<r<=1 formal |Q|^{r-2} is not integrable, but moving coordinates at each simple boundary root make the twice-differentiated norm moment holomorphic for Re r>-1, extending the r>1 identity by analyticity. Finite-dimensional polarization and continuity yield multivariate little-o; Jensen gives r=0. Independently integrated actual perturbed polynomials in n=2,3,5 and r=.5,1,2,4; ratios agreed at small epsilon.
